However, the receiver's onReceive method does not appear to call getAction to ensure that the received Intent's action string matches the expected value, potentially making it possible for another actor to send a spoofed intent with no action string or a different action string and cause undesired behavior. In this case, it is possible that the onReceive method passed the received Intent to another method that checked the action string. If so, this finding can safely be ignored.
